newsitem.title: VIETNAM: India seeks to raise share in world coffee trade.
newsitem.headline: India seeks to raise share in world coffee trade.

text.p: India will strengthen its export programme for coffee to raise its share of the world market, the chairman of the India Coffee Board (ICB) said on Wednesday.
"India hopes to increase its share of the world market," ICB chair Philipose Matthai told an Asia International Coffee conference in Vietnam.
He said this would be done by "bringing in more areas under coffee" to boost production.
The ICB will also initiate visits by trade delegations to target markets and organise Indian coffee festivals in those countries.
The ICB is looking closely at instant coffee as a way to reverse what it calls stagnant domestic consumption.
"We propose to aggressively promote liquid coffee in forms other than the South Indian filter coffee in the non-traditional areas with the active involvement of the private sector."
"Even a marginal increase in the per capita consumption of coffee will fully sustain our industry," he said.

India coffee production in the 1995/96 (October-September) season was estimated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) last month to reach 3.2 million 60 kilogram bags against 3.7 million bags in the previous season.
